source: Round-12 session log: the citation linter's first commit landed via an unintended [skip-cite] match — its own help text mentioned the token by name and the substring check matched it. Fixed in PR #155 follow-up by anchoring the marker to start-of-line.

input.commit_message:
feat(harness): add citation-linter and commit-msg hook

This adds scripts/harness/lib/citation-linter.ts. The CLI prints help
describing accepted exemptions, including the [skip-cite] marker which
power users can place at the start of a line.

The scope=harness exemption applies to tooling commits.

notes: The bug: a pre-anchor regex saw the literal string '[skip-cite]' inside the body's help-text reference and exempted the commit on that basis instead of on the legitimate scope=harness exemption. The fix: SKIP_TOKEN_RE is now `/^\[skip-cite(?::[^\]]*)?]/m` (start-of-line anchored, multiline mode) AND the scope/type checks run first so the right reason wins. Both halves of the fix matter — if either regresses, this case catches it. The expected exempt reason is 'exempt commit scope harness' (NOT the [skip-cite] marker), proving both the anchoring fix and the ordering fix are intact.
